svg.title: Four terms, in plain English
svg.desc: A glossary card with four entries. C corporation: a company that is a taxpayer in its own right, paying tax on its profits before anything reaches its owners. LLC: a company whose profits pass through untaxed to its owners, who pay the tax on their personal returns. Dividend: a share of the company's profits paid out to its owners in cash. Venture fund: a pool of money, largely from pension funds, university endowments and foreign institutions, that buys stakes in startups.

g.text: A company that is a taxpayer in its own right.
It pays tax on its profits before its owners see any.
A company whose profits pass straight to its owners,
untaxed. The owners pay the tax on their own returns.
